summary.name: Garage
summary.one_liner: Garage is a self-contained, S3-compatible distributed object store designed to run across multiple datacenters and low-cost machines.
use_cases: running object storage on second-hand hardware
storage for applications expecting an S3 API
summary.what_it_does: Garage implements the Amazon S3 API so applications already built for S3 can use it. It replicates each chunk of data across 3 zones, with each zone made of multiple servers. It ships as a single dependency-free binary that runs on Linux distributions. The project states it is designed to run over the Internet across multiple datacenters without a dedicated network backbone, and to tolerate network failures, latency, and disk failures. Stated minimum requirements are an x86_64, ARMv7, or ARMv8 CPU, 1 GB RAM, at least 16 GB disk, and a network of 200 ms latency or less with 50 Mbps or more.
notable: Single dependency-free binary designed to run on heterogeneous, second-hand hardware
Three-zone replication of each data chunk
Low stated hardware requirements (1 GB RAM)
Built on research from Dynamo, CRDTs, and Maglev
caveats: Page does not describe a paid tier; funding is from public grants, with donations and support contracts offered
Listing describes the license as AGPL-3.0 and Docker/Rust, but the page text itself does not state these
